rule: 7-day median resting HR 3-5 bpm above the 60-day median -> Yellow (metcon/threshold -> Z2, strength kept)
summary: The direction is supported for short-term overload (RHR rises, small-moderate effect), but the effect is small and inside day-to-day variability, and in functionally overreached triathletes resting HR actually fell, so a normal RHR does not rule out fatigue. No study validates a 3 bpm cut-off; Whoop RHR accuracy is moderate. The Yellow consequence is mild (strength kept), so a heuristic number is acceptable.

sources.note: Meta-analysis: resting HR rose with short-term overload (SMD 0.55) but effects small and within day-to-day noise
Functionally overreached triathletes showed lower resting HR and higher HRV (parasympathetic hyperactivity), not an RHR rise
Whoop 4.0 nocturnal RHR showed only moderate agreement with ECG
